  WHY: A future regression that drops `triage_report_routing_unverified` from the routing gate block (or moves it past the collect header) would still pass `test_routing_contract`, so the structural guard for that contract is silently lost.
- Requirement: "Otherwise log routing_unverified, send a WARNING, and exit without filing an issue."
  Expected change site: `scripts/check_failure_triage.sh`, between the duplicate-issue detection block (lines ~540–542) and the PR-head route verification block (lines ~552–558 in the LAST RUN DIFF; the duplicate exit lives at `if [ -n "${EXISTING}" ]; then ... exit 0 fi`, route verification is the `routing_result=""` block guarded by `PR_HEAD_ROUTING_ENABLED`).
  Evidence of absence: With `CHECK_TRIAGE_PR_HEAD_ROUTING_ENABLED=true`, a run that reaches the duplicate check while the PR payload fetch failed (so `PR_STATE` is empty and the early `pr_not_open` / `fork_pr` exits do not trigger) will satisfy `[ -n "${EXISTING}" ]` and `exit 0` before the route verification at line ~552 ever runs, so neither `triage_report_routing_unverified` nor the Telegram WARNING fires. The LAST RUN DIFF closes the early-exit gap and the lineage-cap gap but not this one. No test covers the "duplicate-issue + unverified-route" combination; `test_collect_flag_on_rejects_unverified_pr_head` does not exercise the duplicate branch.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
